comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's AI strategy is focused on three priorities: delivering a broad portfolio of high-performance adaptive hardware and software solutions, expanding ecosystem partnerships to accelerate deployments, and providing compelling user experiences via the open ROCm software platform.
comparisons.comparison: NVIDIA and AMD both emphasize AI hardware and software strategies involving ecosystem partnerships, but they differ in their specific focus areas. NVIDIA's autonomous vehicle strategy is detailed as a specific vertical application ('DRIVE brand') relying on neural networks for perception and planning, involving partnerships with OEMs and tier-1 suppliers. AMD's AI strategy is described more broadly across its portfolio, focusing on delivering 'adaptive hardware and software solutions' and expanding ecosystem partnerships to accelerate deployments at scale. While NVIDIA's partnership focus is explicitly automotive OEMs/suppliers for AVs, AMD's partnership discussion is general to AI solutions without specific automotive vehicle platform details in this disclosure.

comparisons.peer_topic: x86 Ecosystem Strategy and Advisory Group
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel's core strategy relies on the x86 ecosystem, advancing it through microarchitectures focused on performance and efficiency. In 2024, the company created an advisory group to expand ecosystem compatibility, simplify software development, and identify future architectural needs.
comparisons.comparison: NVIDIA and Intel both identify autonomous driving as a key emerging field and application area for their computing solutions. NVIDIA describes its strategy as providing a specific 'AI-based hardware and software solution' for the AV market, noting that legacy approaches are insufficient for complex neural network algorithms. Intel similarly lists 'autonomous driving' among the fields its products serve, scaling from data center to edge computing. However, NVIDIA's disclosure is specific to an end-to-end autonomous platform (DRIVE), whereas Intel's disclosure positions autonomous driving as one of several verticals served by its broader x86 and xPU ecosystem strategy, without detailing a dedicated autonomous brand or solution suite in this text.

sentences.text: Therefore, we provide an AI-based hardware and software solution, designed and implemented from the ground up based on automotive safety standards, for the AV and EV market under the DRIVE brand, which we are bringing to market through our partnerships with automotive OEMs, tier-1 suppliers, and start-ups.
The algorithms required for autonomous driving - such as perception, localization, and planning - are too complex for legacy hand-coded approaches and will use multiple neural networks instead.

Our product offerings provide end-to-end solutions, scaling from data center to network, PCs, edge computing, and the emerging fields of AI and autonomous driving, to serve an increasingly smart and connected world.

comparisons.peer_topic: Automotive Market Trends and Product Qualifications
comparisons.peer_summary: Demand for automotive memory is driven by autonomous driving, advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), and in-vehicle infotainment. In 2024, the company qualified automotive LPDDR5X, UFS 3.1, and NOR flash solutions for cloud-connected platforms designed for power data-rich, intelligent automotive services.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and Micron disclose specific strategies and product qualifications targeting the autonomous vehicle and automotive memory markets. NVIDIA focuses on providing a comprehensive AI-based hardware and software platform (DRIVE) utilizing neural networks for perception and planning, alongside the hardware required to train these networks. In contrast, Micron focuses on the underlying memory and storage components, noting that demand is driven by autonomous driving and ADAS. Micron highlights qualifying specific memory solutions (LPDDR5X, UFS 3.1, NOR flash) for cloud-connected automotive platforms, whereas NVIDIA provides the compute architecture that likely consumes such memory, emphasizing the complexity of autonomous algorithms that require its specific AI hardware solutions.

sentences.text: In addition, EV makers are looking for next-generation centralized car computers that integrate a wide range of intelligent functions into a single AI compute platform.

Therefore, we provide an AI-based hardware and software solution, designed and implemented from the ground up based on automotive safety standards, for the AV and EV market under the DRIVE brand, which we are bringing to market through our partnerships with automotive OEMs, tier-1 suppliers, and start-ups.

Automotive: Advancements in autonomous driving, advanced driver-assistance systems, and in-vehicle infotainment systems continue to increase the requirements for high-performing memory and storage products, with higher reliability requirements for leading-edge products.

In 2024, we qualified our automotive LPDDR5X, UFS 3.1, and NOR flash storage solutions for a comprehensive set of cloud-connected platforms designed for power data-rich, intelligent automotive services.

comparisons.peer_summary: Digitalization of the automotive cockpit and car-to-cloud platforms are transforming the in-vehicle experience and driving software-defined vehicle architecture.
comparisons.comparison: NVIDIA and Qualcomm both address the transformation of the automotive industry through digitalization and advanced computing, though they emphasize different layers of the vehicle architecture. NVIDIA explicitly mentions partnerships with OEMs and suppliers to bring its DRIVE brand to market for AVs and EVs. Qualcomm details the shift toward 'software-defined vehicle' architectures driven by digital cockpits and car-to-cloud platforms with over-the-air (OTA) update capabilities. While NVIDIA's disclosure includes hardware for 'over-the-air software updates' of neural networks, Qualcomm focuses on the broader vehicle lifecycle management and user experience personalization enabled by connectivity, complementing the compute and sensing functions provided by peers like NVIDIA.

sentences.text: Therefore, we provide an AI-based hardware and software solution, designed and implemented from the ground up based on automotive safety standards, for the AV and EV market under the DRIVE brand, which we are bringing to market through our partnerships with automotive OEMs, tier-1 suppliers, and start-ups.

Our AV solution also includes the GPU-based hardware required to train the neural networks before their in-vehicle deployment, as well as to re-simulate their operation prior to any over-the-air software updates.

Digitalization of the automotive cockpit including wireless connectivity continues to transform the in-vehicle experience, enabling greater personalization of content and settings for both drivers and passengers as automakers respond to growing interest from consumers to bring their digital lifestyles into the vehicle.

Car-to-cloud platforms are designed to help automakers improve cost efficiencies, create new service opportunities throughout the lifecycle of a vehicle with over-the-air (OTA) update capabilities and gather valuable vehicle and usage analytics.
